name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since 5 Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms limits since New START lapsed; US alone opposed a UN test-ban resolution; IAEA flags Iran on 13 Nov
state: New START expired on 5 Feb with no replacement, and the US was the only state to oppose a UN First Committee resolution on the test-ban treaty's entry into force before the session closed on 3 Nov, while saying it keeps a zero-yield testing moratorium (Arms Control Association, 6 Nov). An IAEA report on 13 Nov says it cannot rule out diversion of Iran's declared nuclear material, and the board meets next week (AFP via Arab News). No nuclear test, change in alert levels or threat of use was found as of 14 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No direct effect on the UK public. This reflects the erosion of arms-control limits rather than an immediate threat; UK government emergency preparedness guidance covers what to do in any national emergency.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired 5 Feb); no test or alert-level change

sources.title: Arms Control Association — U.S. opposes key UN disarmament resolutions
Arab News (AFP) — UN nuclear watchdog urges Iran to take steps towards inspections

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
